newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber softens in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber softens in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were generally lower in late trading on Monday on continued thin buying interest, traders said.
"All traders are frustrated today because prices continue to fall," said one trader.

"There were deals taking place in Palembang but traders in other cities did not like it because the prices there are very low. They refused to sell and wish to wait a little bit longer," he added. Traders said Singaporean dealers bought SIR20 at 47.675 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for June shipment. Rubber was offered at 48.25 in the city last week.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 48.25 fob Medan against 48.50 last week and at 47.75 fob Padang against 48.00, but levels were unchanged fob Surabaya at 48.00.
They said offer prices were generally stable at 47.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.

"Traders do not have any short-term plans now. They are just waiting to see what will happen in the market in the coming days. Many believe prices will fall to 45.00 U.S. cents/lb," said another trader.
